name: Pipilotti Rist
bio: Pipilotti Rist (born 1962) studied commercial art, illustration and photography in Vienna and video in Basel, and played in the band Les Reines Prochaines. Her early single-channel videos, such as I'm Not The Girl Who Misses Much (1986), distort pop songs and her own body; Ever Is Over All (1997), in which a woman smashes car windows with a flower while a police officer salutes, won a prize at the Venice Biennale. She went on to fill whole rooms with projected colour: Pour Your Body Out (7354 Cubic Meters) took over MoMA's atrium in 2008, and Pixel Forest (2016) hangs thousands of LEDs like rain. She also works in public space: a bright pink tram for Geneva, a red rubber 'city lounge' in St. Gallen (with Carlos Martinez), illuminated lamp sculptures. Her one feature film, Pepperminta, was released in 2009.
studyNotes: Same sensibility, any medium. Song, single-channel video, room-sized projection, furniture, a tram, a public square: the colour, humour and bodily closeness stay the same.
Design the viewer's body. She adds sofas, carpets, cushions and beds so people lie down and look up; posture changes how video is watched.
Projection meets architecture. Images are thrown onto ceilings, corners, objects and floors instead of a screen; look for how the edges of the image are handled.
Joy as a critical tool. Pleasure and playfulness are used to question how women's bodies are shown, not just to entertain.
